P1 — `scripts/m381_bit13_noun.py:151-176` (`G0`) does not gate the “both setters call `FUN_00551a20`” claim.

`G0` asserts that `FUN_00502cd0` contains exactly two `push 0x2000` sites and that `0x50393d` is followed by `call 0x551a20`, but it never asserts that `0x506cf1` is followed by `call 0x551a20`. The evidence prints the `0x506cf1` sequence, but the gate would still pass if setter B’s call target changed, if the call moved outside the 4-instruction window, or if the second stamp stopped feeding the relations setter. `NAMED.md` row 1 is marked `V MU1 MU6`, but both mutants attack setter A (`0x50393d` / `0x503944`), not setter B. This is a verified claim not actually read by the cited gate.

P1 — `scripts/m381_bit13_noun.py:167-176` (`G0`) does not gate setter B’s “only guard is `test BYTE [row(edi,esi)],0x10 / jne`”.

The gate only checks that the 8-instruction window before `0x506cf1` does not contain `0x94e48c`. It prints the guard window but never asserts the `test BYTE PTR [...],0x10` / `jne` pair, never asserts the row is `row(edi,esi)`, and never asserts that this is the only guard. `MU13` only smuggles a `0x94e48c` operand into the window; it does not mutate the positive guard. So the “not at war only” claim is under-gated and can stay green if setter B’s guard changes to something else that still lacks `0x94e48c`.

P1 — `NAMED.md` M381 evidence citations are wrong for several rows.

Using the shipped `evidence/m381_bit13_noun.txt` line numbering:

- setter A guard cites `:8-11`, but those lines are setter B / `G0` evidence; setter A is `G1` around `:13-15`.
- setter B guard cites `:12-13`, but those are blank / `G1` header; setter B guard is `:8-10`.
- both-rows-written cites `:44-47`, but `:44` is `ok G5` and `:46-47` are `G6`; the mask/tail evidence is `:38-44`.
- readers cites `:57-60`, but `:57` is `ok G7` and `:59-60` are `G8`; reader evidence is `:54-57`.

Repo convention requires claims to cite the evidence line that reads the fact. These citations point at adjacent or unrelated sections, so the audit trail is broken even where the script may measure something.

P2 — `scripts/m381_bit13_noun.py:297-330` (`G5`) gates the caller stamp, not the callee mask claim named by `NAMED.md` row 6.

`G5` checks that `0x50393d` pushes `0x2000` and `0x503944` calls `0x551a20`, then it checks the callee’s six dword AND masks and two `or edx,ebx` tail sites. But the named mutants `MU1` and `MU6` only mutate the caller push/call. There is no mutant that changes one of the callee AND masks to clear bit 13, changes the dword-mask count, or removes/repoints `0x551be6` / `0x551c09`. The “all 6 dword AND masks preserve bit 13” and “tail ORs both rows” facts are therefore not proven by the harness row that claims them.

P2 — `scripts/m381_bit13_noun.py:333-360` (`G6`) does not gate the “attitude delta adds” part of the follow-on claim.

`G6` checks the caller base immediate `0x94f504`, the `0x800000` test, the pushed delta `3`, the clamp immediate `0x14`, and one callee head load from `0x94d488`. It never checks that `FUN_00531b0` adds the delta or stores the clamped result. `NAMED.md` row 7 says “adds to `[a,b]+0x94d488`, clamp `0x14`”, but the shipped mutant `MU5` only shifts the caller stat base. The callee add/store semantics are printed as prose but not read by a failing mutation.

P2 — `scripts/m381_bit13_noun.py:363-397` (`G7`) does not gate the “0x555747 leaves the bit-31 clear unexecuted” control-flow claim.

`G7` asserts the reader census and that `0x555750` is `and eax,0x7fffffff`, but it does not assert that `0x555747`’s `test ah,0x20` branches around `0x555750`, nor that the clear is conditional on bit 13 being clear. The claim is about execution behavior (“leaves ... unexecuted”), while the gate only checks that the clear instruction exists nearby. `MU7` changes the reader mask and reddens the census, but it does not test the skip relationship.

P2 — `scripts/m381_bit13_noun.py:232-262` (`G2`) overstates “`+esi` appears only in the two relations chains”.

`G2` checks that the strength chain has no `add eax,esi` and that the two named control sites `0x5038f4` and `0x50390f` do add `esi`. It does not census the loop, function, or image for other `add eax,esi` occurrences. The printed line “where +esi DOES appear” is hardcoded. The claim’s “only” is therefore not measured; a third `+esi` chain elsewhere in the same loop/function would not redden `G2`.

P2 — `scripts/m381_bit13_noun.py:363-376` (`G7`) uses an undisclosed 3-instruction load window for the reader census.

Both byte-form and dword-form reader detection only counts a `test ah,0x20` or `test/and reg,0x2000` if one of the previous three parsed instructions contains `94d448`. The prose claim says “readers: 5 byte-form ... + 1 dword-form”, which reads like an exhaustive relations-dword reader census, but the instrument’s definition silently caps the load-to-test distance. If a real reader loads the relations dword four or more instructions before testing bit 13, it is invisible to the gate. The measurement definition needs to match the claim or disclose the window.

P2 — `scripts/m381_bit13_noun.py:180-229` (`G1`) calls the window “byte-exact” but only compares mnemonic/operand text.

`G1` says “byte-exact” and evidence says “69 instructions pinned, 0 mismatched”, but the comparison uses normalized `mn + ops`, not the instruction bytes. It does not verify the actual byte encodings except in unrelated `G4` prints. If the claim is that the instruction stream is byte-exact, the gate should compare `INS[...]["b"]` or otherwise read bytes; otherwise the evidence wording should be downgraded to “instruction-text exact”.
